avis.titre: Product is 5 Stars; The Pump's Nozzle is 0.
avis.texte: This is the profound issue with companies using focus groups and places like Influenster instead of trusting the opinions of their actual customers. Those people are literally incentivized to lie. They post their 5 star reviews of an unopened product next to flowers or something corny and rush off to sell it on Mercari. If they were actually honest they'd have pointed out the huge flaw in this design. The nozzle is way too short resulting in product spilling down the top forcing people to wipe it off of the bottle and apply it from there. I'm sure Tatcha's goal is to make sure we're still going to spend our money but none of us actually believe the incentivized reviews. So I end up feeling like a paying product tester. I don't know why they can't select a random group of customers for product testing. If the product is good, they'll repurchase anyway. I do love the product as with all Tatcha products - one look at my vanity is a clear example of my loyalty to these products. However, this isn't the first time there's been issues with product housing that could've been addressed before the final release.
